lines: Put it down! Three wishes. Don't make one.
This isn't an old legend. In 1902, the English writer W. W. Jacobs wrote the story of the most dangerous gift in England.
A soldier brought it home from India. An old holy man had cursed it, to show that fate punishes anyone who meddles.
Three men can have three wishes each. The first man's last wish... was for death.
He threw it on the fire. The father of the house pulled it back out.
The paw twisted in his hand like a snake. And then... nothing.
The next day, their son was caught in the machines at work.
The firm takes no blame. But they wish to give you... 200 pounds.
Ten days later, the mother grabbed the paw.
Wish him back! Bring our boy back!
He'd been in the ground for ten days.
That night... something knocked at the door.
The father crawled through the dark, found the paw... and made his last wish.
The knocking stopped. The door swung open. The road was empty.
Just one tiny wish. I wish Grandma would let me keep it.
